 Satyen Vaidya, Judge

This appeal has been filed under Section 30 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 (for short 'the Act') against the award dated 15.05.2014 passed by the Commissioner, Workmen Compensation (for short 'the Commissioner') in case No. 22 of 2011, whereby the respondents No.1 to 3 (hereinafter referred to as 'the claimants') have been awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.8,06,440/- along-with interest @ 12% per annum w.e.f.
1
Whether the reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

Yes. 
2 ( 2025:HHC:26497 ) 11.03.2009 till the realization and Rs.5,000/- as funeral charges.

2. The claimants had filed claim petition under .
Section 22 of the Act for compensation on account of death of Mukesh Kumar in the course of his employment with respondent No.4 herein (hereinafter referred to as 'the employer').
It was alleged that Mukesh Kumar was employed as driver by the employer to drive tempo No.PB-07J-4680.
On 11.02.2009, the said tempo while being driven by Mukesh Kumar met with an accident, resulting in his death.

sentences.text: The claimants had alleged that deceased Mukesh Kumar was being paid Rs.4,000/- per month as salary besides Rs.200/- per day as expenses.

4. The vehicle i.e. tempo No.PB-07J-4680 was stated to have been insured with the appellant (hereinafter referred to as the 'insurer').
5.
The employer did not choose to contest the petition and was proceeded against ex-parte.
6. The insurer had contested the petition on the ground that the employer had not informed the insurer regarding the employment of deceased Mukesh Kumar.

It was also alleged that Mukesh Kumar was not holding a valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle involved in the 3 (
2025:HHC:26497 ) accident.
The factum of insurer having insured the tempo No.PB-07J-4680 was also denied.
7. Learned Commissioner framed the following issues .

vide order dated 31.05.2010:-
1.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

OPP.
2.
Whether the claim petition is not maintainable ?
OPR2 3.
Whether the deceased was not holding valid & effective driving license ?
OPR2 4.
Whether the vehicle was not insured with respondent No.2 at the time of accident?
r OPR2 5.
Whether the vehicle was being plied by violating the terms and of insurance policy, if any ?

OPR2.
6. Relief.
8.
All the issues except issue No.1 were decided in negative.
The petition was allowed and the claimants have been awarded compensation as noticed above.

9. The appeal was admitted on the following substantial questions of law:-
i) Whether the award of the Commissioner suffers from illegality and is unsustainable in the absence of necessary issues regarding employer-employee relationship and the deceased dying during the course of his employment under the insured?
National Insurance Company vs Mamta Devi And Others on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68988071/
2 ii) Whether the award is unsustainable for the reason that the Commissioner had fallen in error while applying the govt. notification/provisions of law with retrospective effect?
iii) Whether the Commissioner had fallen into error while holding insurance company liable to satisfy the claim in 4 ( 2025:HHC:26497 ) spite of the fact the violation of policy terms and conditions having been fully proved on record?
10.

I have heard learned counsel for the parties and .
have also gone through the records of the case carefully.
11. Mr. Deepak Bhasin, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Mr.Sambhav Bhasin, Advocate has contended that the impugned award was not sustainable on three counts.

Firstly, that the relationship of employee and employer was not established between the deceased Mukesh Kumar and the employer; secondly, it was proved in the statement of RW-1 that licence held by the deceased Mukesh Kumar was to drive LMV only and lastly, that the income of the deceased Mukesh Kumar was wrongly assessed at Rs.8,000/- per month.

12. Learned Commissioner by placing reliance on the statement of claimant Mamta Devi (PW-1) has held that deceased Mukesh Kumar was employee of the employer and his death had taken place during the course of his employment.
13. On behalf of the claimants, only one witness i.e. PW-1 Mamta Devi was examined.

On the other hand, the insurer also examined only one witness i.e. licence Clerk from the office of SDM,
Hamirpur.
This witness had produced the 5 ( 2025:HHC:26497 ) record of licence held by deceased Mukesh Kumar, according to which deceased was authorised to drive Light Motor Vehicle.
PW-1 Mamta Devi had specifically stated on oath that her husband deceased Mukesh Kumar was working as driver with the employer for last about 15 years.

She also deposed that deceased had driven the tempo from Jalandhar to Palampur to deliver consignment and while on his route back from Palampur to Jalandhar, the tempo met with an accident on 11.02.2009.
15.
As against this testimony, nothing else had been placed on record to belie the version of the claimants.
16. It was not the case of the insurer that deceased Mukesh Kumar had not died in the accident involving tempo No.PB-07J-4680.
It was also not alleged that deceased Mukesh Kumar was not driving the tempo at the time of accident.
Even the ownership of tempo with the employer was not in dispute.

That being so, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, the version of claimants has rightly been believed by the learned Commissioner while holding that deceased Mukesh Kumar was employee of the employer and had died during the course of his employment.

sentences.text:
As regard the validity of driving licence of deceased, the insurer itself has proved on record that driving licence Ext.RW-1/A belonged to deceased Mukesh Kumar and .
was valid for driving the Light Motor Vehicle.

18. The Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Company Vs Rambha devi and others 2025(3) SCC 95 has held that the holder of licence to drive the Light Motor Vehicle can drive transport vehicle with the gross vehicle weight less than 7500 kilograms.

entities.text: Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Company Vs Rambha devi and others 2025(3) SCC 95
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. In the facts and circumstances of the instant case, weight of the vehicle i.e. tempo No.PB-07J-4680 has not been proved to be above 7500 kilograms.
Thus, the objection raised by the insurer deserves rejection.

20. The third contention of the insurer, however, deserves to be allowed for the reason that date of accident is 11.02.2009, whereas, the learned Commissioner has given the benefit of Notification No.S.O.1258 (E) dated 31.05.2010 issued by the Government of India raising maximum cap of wages/salary of workman to Rs.8,000/- from Rs.4,000/-.
21.
It is no longer res-integra that a person becomes entitled to compensation under the Act on the date on which cause of action arises
. In this case, the cause of action arose 7 ( 2025:HHC:26497 ) on 11.02.2009.

On the date of accident, the maximum wages of the victim employee could not be considered more than Rs.4,000/-, in terms of explanation (II) appended to Section 4 .
of the Act.
The subsequent raising of limit of Rs.8,000/- by Notification dated 31.05.2010 could not have been allowed retrospectively.

Reference in this regard can be made to the judgments passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pratap Narain Singh Deo vs. Srinivas Sabata and another (1976) 1 SCC 289;Kerala State Electricity Board and another vs. Valsala K. and another (1999) 8 SCC 254 and also K. Sivaraman and others vs. P. Sathishkumar and another (2020) 4 SCC 594.
22.

sentences.text: Thus, the income of deceased Mukesh Kumar could not have been taken for the purposes of computation of compensation beyond Rs.4,000/- per month.

In terms of Section 4(i) (a) of the Act,
50% was to be considered as monthly wages for being multiplied with the relevant factor of 201.66.

In this manner, the compensation payable to the claimants would be Rs.2000 X 201.66= Rs.
4,03,220/-.
23.

The statutory interest has rightly been awarded to the claimants @ 12% per annum w.e.f.
11.03.2009 and no interference is required to be made to that extent.

Similarly, 8 (
2025:HHC:26497 ) Rs.5,000/- awarded on account of funeral charges shall remain unchanged.
24. In result, the appeal is partly allowed.
